title: Weekly Scientific Lineage · 2026-W47
executive_summary:
The week follows the causal chain from compact central engines and their magnetic or accretion loading, through jets, winds, and circumburst or binary plasma, to the clocks, spectra, damping, and multi-messenger signatures used to infer the engine.
- **Repeating FRBs and changing environments**: arXiv:2611.17805 finds a $\sim120\,\mathrm{d}$ modulation of the daily-mean linear polarization fraction of FRB 20240114A, with phase-distance correlation peaking at $P=119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}\,\mathrm{d}$ and a folded semi-amplitude of $3.23\%$, while a $95\%$ bound $\sigma_{\rm RM}<0.51\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$ lowers the degree of linear polarization by only $\sim0.42\%$ at $1.0\,\mathrm{GHz}$ and a $120\,\mathrm{d}$ spin stores only $E_{\rm rot}\simeq1.84\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}$.
- **FRB activity lifetimes beyond the monitoring window**: arXiv:2611.17833 shows that strong lensing by MACS J0717.5+3745 turns image delays into a source-frame activity baseline, with $L_{95}\simeq42.6\,\mathrm{yr}$ for a $T_{\mathrm{obs}}\doteq5\,\mathrm{yr}$ survey at $z_s=2$ and $\mathrm{E}[\ln B_{12}]>3$ when activity durations differ by about one decade.
- **Burst subclasses across FRB active episodes**: arXiv:2611.18056 uses UMAP and HDBSCAN on FRB 20121102A to isolate a high-energy cluster whose episode fraction falls from $26.9^{+2.3}_{-2.2}\%$ in 2019 to $7.7^{+3.1}_{-2.3}\%$ and $7.8^{+6.4}_{-3.7}\%$ in 2022 and 2023, while all clusters keep bandwidth ratio $<0.4$ and similar bimodal waiting times.
- **Merger jets and seconds-long soft X-ray pulses**: arXiv:2611.18210 identifies EP260411a as the sole astrophysical match to short GRB 260411A, with $T_{\rm X,90}=6.1_{-1.1}^{+0.7}\,\mathrm{s}$, $T_{\gamma,90}=1.3_{-0.3}^{+0.2}\,\mathrm{s}$, $w\propto E^{-0.24}$ and $t_{\rm peak}\propto E^{-0.56}$, and places the joint spectrum in the Type I region of the $E_{\rm p,z}$–$E_{\rm iso}$ plane.
- **Surface fields of central compact objects**: arXiv:2611.17430 finds that the $\sim0.7$ and $1.4\,\mathrm{keV}$ lines of 1E 1207.4-5209 imply a steady $B\approx(7\text{–}8)\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{G}$ from 2001 to 2020, consistent with the spin-down value $\approx9.8\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{G}$, with only a rotational contrast $\sim5\times10^{9}\,\mathrm{G}$.
- **Accreting neutron-star spin equilibrium**: arXiv:2611.17972 describes 39 LMXB spins as a broad slow component plus a narrow pileup at $\mu_{\rm G}=565.7\,\mathrm{Hz}$ with $\sigma_{\rm G}=32.4\,\mathrm{Hz}$, shows that ordinary torque diffusion supplies only $\Delta\nu_{\rm diff}\simeq7.9\,\mathrm{Hz}$, and requires $B\propto\dot{M}^{1/2}$ if the fast peak is not to be broadened by accretion-rate scatter.
- **Non-ultracompact but helium-rich burst fuel**: arXiv:2611.18226 finds that a $P_{\rm orb}\approx3.47\,\mathrm{hr}$ neutron-star LMXB produces $7$–$10\,\mathrm{s}$ non-PRE bursts with $\alpha=114\pm14$ and ignition models favoring $X\sim0.03$ and $Z_{\rm CNO}\approx4\times10^{-4}$.
- **Resonant dark-matter trapping in supernovae**: arXiv:2611.17604 argues that nonresonant $\nu\bar\nu\to\chi\bar\chi$ production combined with resonant $\chi\bar\nu$ scattering opens an SN1987A cooling gap from about $5\,\mathrm{MeV}$ to $100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ at $m_\phi=3m_\chi$, relative to the Raffelt limit $5\times10^{52}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$.
- **Suprathermal damping in merger remnants**: arXiv:2611.18146 shows that $1\,\mathrm{kHz}$ oscillations with $\Delta n/n\sim0.1$ drive $|\mu_\Delta|/T\geq1$ and can raise the bulk viscosity by up to five orders of magnitude above the subthermal value at $T=0.5\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
- **Kink-mediated baryon loading of magnetized jets**: arXiv:2611.18268 shows that unloaded magnetic acceleration would reach $\Gamma_j\sim10^{4}$ near $100\,\mathrm{pc}$, whereas a kink at a $\sigma=10^{3}$ jet–wind interface mixes plasma until the relaxed volume average satisfies $\langle\sigma\rangle<1$.

overview_matrix.domain: Repeating FRBs: polarization clocks, activity lifetimes, and emission subclasses
overview_matrix.key_question: Do hundred-day polarization cycles, lensing time delays, and episode-dependent burst subclasses trace a binary or circumburst screen, a long-lived engine duty cycle, or changing emission-region conditions?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2611.17805]: Daily-mean degree of linear polarization of FRB 20240114A peaks at $P=119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ (phase-distance correlation $0.1452$ versus a $99\%$ global threshold $0.1262$) and $122.31\,\mathrm{d}$ in the generalized Lomb–Scargle periodogram; folding gives a $3.23\%$ semi-amplitude. For $M_{\rm tot}=10M_\odot$ the implied separation is $a\simeq1.03\,\mathrm{au}$. Internal Faraday depolarization is only $\sim0.42\%$ and $0.083\%$ at $1.0$ and $1.5\,\mathrm{GHz}$, and $E_{\rm rot}\simeq1.84\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}$ rules out a $120\,\mathrm{d}$ spin as the burst engine.
- [arXiv:2611.17833]: For $T_{\mathrm{act}}=100\,\mathrm{yr}$, $z_s=2$, and $\lambda_0=0.1\,\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{src}}^{-1}$, a $5\,\mathrm{yr}$ survey reaches $m_{95}\simeq25.6$ and $L_{95}\simeq42.6\,\mathrm{yr}$; the catalog envelope is $79.29$ source-frame years, with one delay set $(0,23.22,42.01)\,\mathrm{yr}$. Delayed images give $G>1$, and activity durations separated by about a decade yield $\mathrm{E}[\ln B_{12}]>3$.
- [arXiv:2611.18056]: Above $E\geq2.5\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg}$, HDBSCAN Cluster 1 contains nearly all high-energy bursts and most events above $T_{\mathrm{B,cri}}\approx10^{33}\,\mathrm{K}$, but its fraction drops from $26.9^{+2.3}_{-2.2}\%$ (2019) to $\sim8\%$ (2022 and 2023). Clusters 2 and 4 have bandwidth ratios $\sim0.1$; every cluster stays below $0.4$ and shares bimodal waiting times, favoring a change in subclass mix rather than a new waiting-time clock.
overview_matrix.significance: A $\sim120\,\mathrm{d}$ polarization cycle is more naturally a binary or slowly changing propagation geometry than a stellar spin, while lensing recovers pre-window activity and the 20121102A subclass shift shows that one repeater can change its high-energy emission mix between episodes.

overview_matrix.domain: Relativistic jets, short GRBs, and magnetized baryon loading
overview_matrix.key_question: Is a few-second soft X-ray pulse the same on-axis post-merger jet as a short GRB, and can a jet–wind kink load enough baryons to stop unloaded magnetic acceleration at $\Gamma_j\sim10^{4}$?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2611.18210]: EP260411a is the only astrophysical candidate matched to GRB 260411A (Li–Ma $S=5.26$; $P_{\rm chance}<2.73\times10^{-3}$ and $P_{\rm chance,global}<1.62\times10^{-2}$ after six trials). Both pulses are FRED, with $T_{\rm X,90}=6.1_{-1.1}^{+0.7}\,\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\gamma,90}=1.3_{-0.3}^{+0.2}\,\mathrm{s}$, and Norris fits give $w\propto E^{-0.24_{-0.02}^{+0.12}}$ and $t_{\rm peak}\propto E^{-0.56_{-0.11}^{+0.06}}$. The joint continuum has $\Gamma_2=1.58\pm0.16$ and $E_{\rm p}=386_{-178}^{+288}\,\mathrm{keV}$ and lies in the Type I $E_{\rm p,z}$–$E_{\rm iso}$ region, favoring one post-merger jet rather than a separate long-lived engine.
- [arXiv:2611.18268]: Unloaded acceleration obeys $\Gamma_j(1+\sigma_j)=\Gamma_0(1+\sigma_0)$, so $\Gamma_j=r_j/r_{lc}$ reaches $\Gamma_j\sim10^{4}$ near $100\,\mathrm{pc}$, above $\Gamma_j\lesssim50$. A $\sigma=10^{3}$ core against a $\sigma_w=0.1$ wind grows a kink slightly faster than $\Gamma_g^{\max}=0.133\,c_a/r_c$ at $\lambda_m=8.43\,r_c$; nonlinearly the interface becomes a helical corkscrew and the relaxed mixture has $\langle\sigma\rangle<1$. For $\sigma_w=10^{-3}$ the mixing is weaker and gaps remain at $\sigma\gtrsim1$.
overview_matrix.significance: EP260411a compresses the usual minutes-long extragalactic-fast-X-ray-transient timescale down to seconds and aligns it with a hard short GRB, while the kink calculation shows that interface mixing, not the base magnetization alone, can set whether a Blandford–Znajek jet stays Poynting-dominated.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: FRB geometry, lifetimes, and episode-dependent emission
thematic_highlights.summary: Three repeater studies separate propagation, engine lifetime, and radiation-state changes. arXiv:2611.17805 measures a $119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ polarization cycle in FRB 20240114A whose $6.46\%$ peak-to-peak amplitude is not produced by the measured RM scatter and whose associated rotational energy is orders of magnitude below $E_{\rm iso}\sim10^{37}$–$10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg}$, pointing to orbital geometry at $a\simeq1.03\,\mathrm{au}$ for $M_{\rm tot}=10M_\odot$. arXiv:2611.17833 shows that a non-detection is not quiescence: MACS J0717.5+3745 delays stretch a $5\,\mathrm{yr}$ campaign to a $42.6\,\mathrm{yr}$ source-frame reach and can distinguish activity durations a decade apart. arXiv:2611.18056 finds that the high-energy, high-brightness-temperature subclass of FRB 20121102A declines from roughly $27\%$ to $8\%$ across the 2019, 2022, and 2023 episodes even though bandwidth ratios remain $<0.4$ and waiting times stay bimodal, so the engine changes its emission-region mix rather than its recurrence clock.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Short-GRB jets and kink-driven baryon loading
thematic_highlights.summary: arXiv:2611.18210 supplies a rare seconds-long soft X-ray counterpart, EP260411a, to short GRB 260411A. The shared FRED morphology, the narrowing $w\propto E^{-0.24}$ and earlier $t_{\rm peak}\propto E^{-0.56}$, and a joint break at $E_{\rm b}=7_{-3}^{+6}\,\mathrm{keV}$ with $E_{\rm p}=386_{-178}^{+288}\,\mathrm{keV}$ place the event with Type I merger jets rather than a distinct long engine. On larger scales, arXiv:2611.18268 shows why such jets cannot remain purely magnetically accelerated: a static $\sigma=10^{3}$ column against a disk wind is Kruskal–Shafranov unstable, grows a helical kink, and mixes down to $\langle\sigma\rangle<1$ when $\sigma_w=0.1$, whereas $\sigma_w=10^{-3}$ leaves highly magnetized coils. The interface density contrast therefore controls whether the terminal Lorentz factor stays near the observed $\Gamma\approx10$ or runs away toward $10^{4}$.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Neutron-star fields, equilibrium spins, and unusual donors
thematic_highlights.summary: arXiv:2611.17430 tracks 1E 1207.4-5209 for two decades and finds no global change in the cyclotron field $B\approx(7\text{–}8)\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{G}$; the $\sim50\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $\sim20\,\mathrm{eV}$ rotational shifts of the two lines are a surface contrast, not evidence that the 2015 glitch restructured the dipole. arXiv:2611.17972 then shows that accreting neutron stars do not fill spin frequency uniformly: a narrow component at $565.7\pm32.4\,\mathrm{Hz}$ contains the fast systems, which also prefer longer orbits, while $\Delta\nu_{\rm diff}\simeq7.9\,\mathrm{Hz}$ is too small for short-timescale torque noise to set the width. arXiv:2611.18226 adds a chemical constraint: at $P_{\rm orb}\approx3.47\,\mathrm{hr}$, burst trains still require $X\sim0.03$ and $Z_{\rm CNO}\approx4\times10^{-4}$, and the long-term flux is below the conservative transfer rate, so a helium-rich donor plus mass loss can mimic ultracompact fuel.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Cooling bounds and viscous damping in compact transients
thematic_highlights.summary: arXiv:2611.17604 changes the supernova-cooling argument for neutrinophilic dark matter: because scattering, not production, is resonant at $s=m_\phi^2$, particles that would otherwise stream out of the $R_\nu\simeq40\,\mathrm{km}$ neutrinosphere can be trapped, leaving a roughly $5$–$100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ gap in the SN1987A exclusion at $m_\phi=3m_\chi$. arXiv:2611.18146 addresses the opposite, dynamical regime inside mergers. Once $|\mu_\Delta|/T\geq1$, modified- and direct-Urca rates in the nucleon-width approximation make $\zeta$ amplitude-dependent; at $1\,\mathrm{kHz}$ and $T\leq1\,\mathrm{MeV}$ the viscosity can exceed the subthermal estimate by one to five orders, while $T=3\,\mathrm{MeV}$ remains close to that limit. Cold post-merger and proto-neutron-star oscillations are therefore the regime where bulk viscosity can alter gravitational-wave damping and ejecta.

top_picks.title: Periodic Modulation of Linear Polarization Fraction in Repeating FRB 20240114A
top_picks.recommendation_reason: A hundred-day polarization clock with an explicit spin-energy veto is directly usable for binary and circumburst models of repeating FRBs.
top_picks.core_insight: The degree of linear polarization varies at $P\approx119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ with semi-amplitude $3.23\%$, while RM scatter and $E_{\rm rot}\simeq1.84\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}$ rule out Faraday smearing and a slow magnetar spin.
top_picks.reading_guide: Start from the phase-distance and Lomb–Scargle global false-alarm tests, then the RM depolarization and rotational-energy limits.

top_picks.recommendation_reason: The static kink calculation isolates how a jet–wind interface can baryon-load a Blandford–Znajek jet before propagation is added.

papers.title: Periodic Modulation of Linear Polarization Fraction in Repeating FRB 20240114A
papers.result: Daily-mean DOL periodograms peak near 120 days: phase-distance correlation reaches 0.1452 at $P=119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ (99% global threshold 0.1262; $3\sigma$ interval $119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}\,\mathrm{d}$), and generalized Lomb–Scargle reaches power 0.1275 at $122.31\,\mathrm{d}$ (threshold 0.1108; interval $122.31^{+2.63}_{-2.82}\,\mathrm{d}$). Daily medians peak at $119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ and $123.55\,\mathrm{d}$, with global FAPs $5.71\times10^{-4}$ and $2.84\times10^{-3}$ (about $3.25\sigma$ and $2.77\sigma$). Folding at $119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ gives semi-amplitude 3.23% (peak-to-peak 6.46%). For $P_{\rm orb}=119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ and $M_{\rm tot}=10M_\odot$, $a\simeq1.03\,\mathrm{au}$. For 18 bright bursts, $\sigma_{\rm RM}<0.51\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$ (95%), so $p_{\rm L}=p_{\rm L,0}\exp[-2\sigma_{\rm RM}^2\lambda^4]$ lowers DOL by only about 0.42% and 0.083% at 1.0 and 1.5 GHz. With $I=10^{45}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^2}$ and $P_{\rm spin}=120\,\mathrm{d}$, $E_{\rm rot}\simeq1.84\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}$, far below $E_{\rm iso}\sim10^{37}$–$10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg}$.
papers.problem: Whether the degree of linear polarization of repeating FRB 20240114A varies periodically over hundreds of days, and whether that variation traces emission geometry or propagation through a changing circumburst or binary environment.
papers.method: After S/N$>20$, 6099 bursts on 95 days spanning MJD 60337.238–60824.896 ($T=487.66\,\mathrm{d}$) are averaged without weights into daily DOL. Trials from 10 to 240 days use $\Delta f=1/(\mathrm{OS}\,T)$ with $\mathrm{OS}=200$ ($\Delta f\approx1.025\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{d}^{-1}$; 9348 frequencies). PDC correlates $a_{ij}=|D_i-D_j|$ with $b_{ij}(P)=\phi_{ij}(P)[P-\phi_{ij}(P)]$; GLS fits $D(t)=C+a\cos(2\pi ft)+b\sin(2\pi ft)$ and uses $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{GLS}}(f)=1-\mathrm{RSS}(f)/\mathrm{RSS}_0$. Global significance uses $10^7$ permutations on fixed dates, $\mathrm{FAP}_{\mathrm{global}}=(r+1)/(M+1)$. Phase folding uses $\phi_i=\mathrm{mod}((t_i-t_0)/P,1)$ and $\mathrm{DOL}(\phi)=C+a\cos(2\pi\phi)+b\sin(2\pi\phi)$.
papers.reason: FRB 20240114A shows a roughly 120 day modulation of its linear polarization fraction, directly constraining emission geometry versus magneto-ionic propagation for a repeating FRB.

papers.title: Probing the Activity History of Repeating Fast Radio Bursts with Cluster Lensing
papers.result: For $T_{\mathrm{act}}=100\,\mathrm{yr}$, $z_s=2$, and $\lambda_0=0.1\,\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{src}}^{-1}$, a $T_{\mathrm{obs}}\doteq 5\,\mathrm{yr}$ survey has $m_{95}\simeq 25.6$ and source-frame span $L_{95}\simeq 42.6\,\mathrm{yr}$. At $z_s=2$ the catalog maximum envelope is $79.29$ source-frame years and one three-image delay set is $(0,23.22,42.01)\,\mathrm{yr}$. The reach is $L_{\mathrm{env}}=(\max_i\Delta_i-\min_i\Delta_i+T_{\mathrm{obs}})/(1+z_s)$ and $G\equiv(1+z_s)L_{\max}/T_{\mathrm{obs}}$, with $G\le 1$ for a single image and $G>1$ once delayed images are used. Activity durations separated by about one decade give $\mathrm{E}[\ln B_{12}]>3$ (Bayes factor above about 20); an impossible short-duration model gives $B_{12}=+\infty$.
papers.problem: Repeating-FRB engines and active lifetimes are uncertain: intermittent activity means a non-detection is not quiescence, and direct monitoring cannot recover emission epochs before the observing window.
papers.method: Cluster strong lensing of MACS J0717.5+3745 is evaluated on 201 CATS v4.1 maps and 128 source positions with the arrival-time surface $t(\boldsymbol{\theta})=\frac{(1+z_l)D_l D_s}{c D_{ls}}\left[\frac{|\boldsymbol{\theta}-\boldsymbol{\beta}|^2}{2}-\psi(\boldsymbol{\theta})\right]$, delays $d_{ji}=(D_{\Delta t}/c)[\phi(\boldsymbol{\theta}_j)-\phi(\boldsymbol{\theta}_i)]$, and arrivals $t_{ik}=(1+z_s)s_k+\Delta_i$. papers.title: Suprathermal bulk viscosity in binary neutron star mergers
papers.result: At oscillation frequency $f=1$ kHz, nonlinear effects appear when $\Delta n/n$ is around $0.1$. For IUF at $n_B=n_0$ and $T=0.5$ MeV, $\zeta$ increases by up to five orders of magnitude with amplitude, and by three orders at $T=1$ MeV; at $T=3$ MeV it stays near the subthermal limit. Above the direct Urca threshold, at $n_B=6n_0$, the increase is up to three orders at $T=0.5$ MeV and one order at $T=1$ MeV. For QMC-RMF3 at $n_B=n_0$ and $6n_0$, $\zeta$ rises by five orders at $T=0.5$ MeV and three orders at $T=1$ MeV. At $n_B=n_0$, $T=1$ MeV, subthermal NWA $\zeta$ is about an order of magnitude above the Fermi-surface modified-Urca value and remains larger for $\Delta n/n=1$. The suprathermal condition is $|\mu_{\Delta}|/T\geq 1$.
papers.problem: Large-amplitude, kHz density oscillations in binary neutron-star mergers and core-collapse supernovae drive npe matter out of flavor equilibrium into the suprathermal regime $|\mu_{\Delta}|/T\geq 1$, where the usual assumption $\mu_{\Delta}\ll T$ fails and the resulting bulk-viscous damping can affect post-merger gravitational waves and ejecta.
papers.method: The core is npe matter with free-streaming neutrinos. Oscillations $n_*=\bar{n}_*+\Delta n_*\sin(\omega t)$ induce $\mu_{\Delta}$ through EoS susceptibilities $B$ and $C$. Net Urca rates in the Nucleon Width Approximation, including thermal blurring and collisional broadening, are fit as $\Gamma^{(\leftrightarrow)}=-\widetilde{\Gamma}T^{\kappa}\mu_{\Delta}\left(1+\sum_{j=1}^{N}\chi_j(\mu_{\Delta}/T)^j\right)$ in all powers of $\mu_{\Delta}/T$. With $A=\mu_{\Delta}/T$, $d=(C/T)(\Delta n_*/n_*)$, and $f=B\widetilde{\Gamma}T^{\kappa}/\omega$, $A(\varphi;d,f)$ is solved and inserted into $\zeta=(TC/(\pi\omega B))(\bar{n}_*/\Delta n_*)\int_0^{2\pi}A\cos\varphi\,d\varphi$ for the IUF and QMC-RMF3 finite-temperature EoSs.
papers.reason: The work quantifies suprathermal Urca bulk viscosity that can damp kHz density oscillations in binary neutron-star mergers and core-collapse supernovae and change ejecta and post-merger signals, but it is microphysical rather than a direct FRB, jet, shock-breakout, or dispersion-measure study.

papers.title: Magnetic kink instability of jet-wind outflows. I. Static column configuration
papers.result: Unloaded magnetic acceleration obeys $\Gamma_j(1+\sigma_j)=\Gamma_0(1+\sigma_0)$, hence $\Gamma_t\approx\sigma_0/2$; with $\Gamma_j=r_j/r_{lc}$ this gives $\Gamma_j\sim10^{4}$ near $100\,\mathrm{pc}$, above observed $\Gamma_j\lesssim50$ (typically $\Gamma\approx10$). The estimated base state is $B_r=7\times10^{7}A_2(\dot{m}/(\eta_{-1}m_{b,9}))^{1/2}(r/r_g)^{-2}\,\mathrm{G}$ and $\sigma=10^{12}(A_2/(a\mu_5))((\dot{m}m_{b,9})/\eta_{-1})^{1/2}(r/r_g)^{-2}$. Linear kink growth falls as the force-free core radius increases and lies slightly above $\Gamma_g^{\max}=0.133\,c_a/r_c$ at $\lambda_m=8.43\,r_c$, with $c_a^{2}=\sigma/(1+\sigma)$. The jet enters exponential growth sooner than the wind. Nonlinearly the interface becomes a helical corkscrew, high- and low-$\sigma$ plasma interpenetrate, and a secondary magnetic Rayleigh–Taylor-like mode appears. Volume-averaged $\langle\sigma\rangle=\langle B^{2}\rangle/\langle w\rangle$ changes by only a factor of a few, and the relaxed mixture has $\langle\sigma\rangle<1$. For $\sigma_w=10^{-3}$ the mixing is weaker, coils remain highly magnetised, and gaps satisfy $\sigma\gtrsim1$.
papers.problem: BZ-driven AGN jets stay extremely magnetised after pair production, so magnetic acceleration without extra baryons would yield $\Gamma_j\sim10^{4}$, in conflict with $\Gamma_j\lesssim50$; the issue is whether a kink at a jet–disk-wind interface can supply the required baryon loading.
papers.method: Static axisymmetric 3D RMHD equilibria are evolved with PERT on a uniform Cartesian mesh: a constant-pitch, nearly force-free core at $\sigma=10^{3}$ inside a denser shell with $\sigma_w=0.1$ ($M_1$–$M_4$, $r_c=1/6$ to $1/2$) or $\sigma_w=10^{-3}$. Balance is $\frac{d}{dr}(p+p_m)+\frac{B_\phi^{2}}{r}=0$, $p_m=(B_z^{2}+B_\phi^{2})/2$, $\bar B_z=B_0\left(1+(r/r_c)^{2}\right)^{-1}$, $\bar B_\phi=\bar B_z(r/r_c)$, and $\sigma=\frac{2(\gamma-1)}{\beta(\gamma+\epsilon^{-1})}$. Growth is tracked with transverse kinetic energy, $V_{r,\max}$ and $\langle\hat B_r\rangle$; modes with $\lambda>2\pi r_c$ are Kruskal–Shafranov unstable.
papers.reason: The paper quantifies how a current-driven kink can mix a high-$\sigma$ relativistic jet with a low-$\sigma$ wind and thereby baryon-load the jet, but the static-column setup overshoots to $\langle\sigma\rangle<1$ and is only an incremental constraint on jet composition.

papers.title: Polarization of strongly lensed gravitational waves as a probe of the lens-induced orientations of electromagnetic counterparts
papers.result: GW polarization is an absolute reference for intrinsic jet orientation: its offset from the apparent jet axis is the lens-induced orientation offset of each image. Images obey $\boldsymbol{\beta}=\boldsymbol{\theta}-\nabla\Psi$ at stationary points of $\tau(\boldsymbol{\theta};\boldsymbol{\beta})=\frac{1}{2}|\boldsymbol{\theta}-\boldsymbol{\beta}|^2-\Psi$, with $\mu_j=1/\det A_j$ and $\Delta\chi_j\equiv\chi_j-\psi\pmod{\pi}$. After ET+CE selection the detected images are 93% doubles, 5% quadruples, and 2% triples (5908 systems; median $z_s=2.3$, median $\theta_E=0.63''$, longest delay 48 days). Median $\sigma_z/(1+z_s)=0.04$, 27% have $\sigma_\psi<10^\circ$, offsets reach tens of degrees, and at most about one third are measurable; quadrupole $\psi$ is useful only for viewing angles $\gtrsim40^\circ$.
papers.problem: Strongly lensed GW images are one-dimensional time series without sky positions, while a resolvable BNS jet does not reveal its intrinsic orientation, so electromagnetic data usually constrain only relative orientations between images.
papers.method: A static thin lens parallel-transports polarization so $\psi$ is invariant. Three image-plane layers use host-arc positions, Fermat delays and magnifications, and $\chi_j=\arg[A_j^{-1}\hat{e}(\chi_s)]\pmod{\pi}$, with $\sigma_{\Delta\chi,j}^2=\sigma_\psi^2+\sigma_{\chi,j}^2+\sigma_\epsilon^2$ and detection when $\max_j S_j\ge3$. Mock BNS events use flat $\Lambda$CDM, a semi-analytic galaxy lens, and a joint nonspinning 3.5PN TaylorF2 Fisher analysis on ET+CE.
